thread:
Alex Chen: Quick proposal — make v2 the default for /generate starting next week, keep v1 for 6 months behind a compatibility flag. Rationale: v2 has better latency and new batching semantics. Thoughts?
Maria Gomez: @Alex Chen important: how do we surface which version served in billing/quotas? Finance needs per-version breakdown for customer invoices.
Samir Patel: We currently only tag model_id. We can add an `api_version` label to telemetry and billing pipeline, but that touches ingestion schemas. Low effort to add to logs, moderate to pipeline.
Kyra Lee: Compatibility note: v2 changes streaming event structure for tool-calling. Many integrations rely on exact shape. If we flip default we either need a compatibility shim or explicit error guidance.
Dave O'Neill: +1 on adding header for backwards compatibility. Suggest `X-Redwood-API-Version: v2` in responses and `X-Redwood-Deprecation-Notice` when v1 is used but deprecated. Also emit metric `api.version.route` with value=v2/v1.
Maria Gomez: Also need dashboard filters — product and support should be able to filter traffic by api version and model. Can we add a per-route breakdown in Console analytic pages?
Samir Patel: Console change is straightforward if the backend provides the new dimension. I'll add `api_version` to the timeseries and top-k tables. UI effort ~2 days.
product-ops: We need a migration plan: email + in-console banner + auto-fallback. Proposed window: 180 days. Banner should link to changelog and sample shim code.
Kyra Lee: For auto-fallback, prefer route-level policy: if client sends `Accept: application/vnd.redwood.v1+json` we honor v1. Otherwise default to v2. That reduces surprise.
Alex Chen: Good call. Let's standardize on content-negotiation header `Accept` for explicit pinning and `X-Redwood-API-Version` for debugging. We'll also support query param `?api_version=` as last resort.
Dave O'Neill: Can we add a transient translation layer on the runtime that maps v2 streaming frames to v1 format when pinned? Should be possible but we need tests. Estimate: 1-2 sprints.
Samir Patel: I'll draft unit tests and a compatibility test harness. Add an e2e job that runs the v1 regression suite against v2 with shim enabled.
product-ops: Communication timeline: 2-week alpha to internal partners, 4-week public beta with clear banner, then default flip. We'll queue rollout PRs after Samir's infra changes land.
Alex Chen: Action items: Samir add telemetry label + pipeline change (JIRA: PLAT-2345), Dave prototyping shim (PLAT-2346), Kyra to write compatibility doc snippets, Maria to update billing dashboard reqs. I'll own rollout schedule + banners. @deploy-bot can you shadow-route 10% to v2 on staging?
[deploy-bot]: Shadow route created: staging /generate -> v2 (10%). Logs + sampling enabled. :robot_face:
Kyra Lee: Draft snippet for `Accept` header to add to docs:
```
Accept: application/vnd.redwood.v2+json
# pin to v1:
Accept: application/vnd.redwood.v1+json
```
Maria Gomez: Minor ask — add a deprecation telemetry event so we can email customers still on v1 at 60/30/7 days before sunsetting.
Alex Chen: Agreed — add `deprecation.notification` events. We'll add email templates and console calls-to-action.
Dave O'Neill: One more thing: quota semantics. If v2 changes tokenization or message envelope, unit consumption might differ. We should normalize billing units to model tokens, not api envelope, and publish a migration matrix.
Samir Patel: I'll generate a sample comparison report (v1 vs v2 tokens per the same prompts) and attach to the migration doc.
Alex Chen: Thanks everyone — looks like rough consensus. I'll collate and send a formal plan to #product and #support tomorrow. :thumbsup:
Maria Gomez: :eyes:
